Task: Write a comprehensive guide to making homemade sourdough bread.

Comprehensive Guide to Making Homemade Sourdough Bread

1. Understanding Sourdough
• Sourdough uses a natural leaven (starter) made from flour and water fermented by wild yeast and lactic‐acid bacteria.  
• Flavor, texture, and keeping quality depend on the balance of yeast activity (CO₂ for rise) and bacterial activity (acids for tang).

2. Equipment Checklist
• Kitchen scale (accuracy matters)  
• Two glass or food-grade plastic jars (for starter)  
• Mixing bowl (non-reactive)  
• Dough scraper or spatula  
• Bench knife  
• Proofing basket (banneton) or colander lined with a floured towel  
• Dutch oven, baking stone, or heavy sheet pan  
• Razor blade or sharp knife for scoring  
• Oven-safe thermometer (optional)

3. Building & Maintaining a Starter (7-10 days)
Day 1: Mix 50 g whole-grain flour + 50 g water (room temp). Cover loosely.  
Day 2: Discard half, feed with 50 g unbleached bread flour + 50 g water.  
Days 3-5: Feed every 24 h. Look for bubbles, slight rise, mild tangy smell.  
Days 6-7: Feed every 12 h. Starter should double in ≤6 h and smell pleasantly sour.  
Maintenance: Keep 50 g starter; feed equal parts water and flour. Refrigerate if baking ≤1×/week, feeding weekly.

4. Sample Formula (One Boule)
Total dough weight ≈ 850 g  
Ingredient | Baker’s % | Grams
Bread flour | 90 | 405
Whole-wheat flour | 10 | 45
Water (65 % hydration) | 65 | 293
Active starter (100 % hydration) | 20 | 90
Salt | 2 | 9

5. Workflow Timeline (Two-Day Process)
Night Before (Levain Build)  
• 20 g mature starter + 40 g water + 40 g flour. Ferment 8–12 h at 70–75 °F.

Day 1
8 am Autolyse: Mix all flour and 260 g of the water. Rest 45 min.  
8:45 am Mix: Add levain and rest of water; pinch in until incorporated. Add salt; squeeze and fold until gluten forms (5 min).  
9 am–1 pm Bulk Fermentation (75 °F): Perform 4 stretch-and-fold sets every 30 min (9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00). Dough should increase 30–50 %.  
1 pm Pre-shape: Turn out, gently round. Rest 20 min uncovered.  
1:20 pm Final Shape: Tight boule or batard. Place seam-side up in floured banneton.  
1:30–5:30 pm Proof: 3–4 h at 75 °F OR retard 12–16 h in fridge (preferred for flavor and scheduling).

Day 2 (if retarded)
7 am Preheat: Place Dutch oven in oven at 500 °F for 45 min.  
7:45 am Score & Bake: Invert loaf onto parchment, score ½-inch deep. Transfer to hot Dutch oven. Bake 20 min covered at 475 °F, then 20–25 min uncovered at 450 °F until crust is deep brown (205–210 °F internal).  
Cool on rack minimum 1 h before slicing.

6. Key Techniques
Autolyse: Hydrates flour, boosts extensibility.  
Stretch-and-Fold: Develops gluten without kneading; traps gas.  
Cold Retard: Slows fermentation, sharpens flavor, improves crust blistering.  
Scoring: Controls oven spring; angle blade 30°.  
Steam: Dutch oven traps steam for glossy crust; alternatively, add water to preheated tray.

7. Troubleshooting
Dense loaf: Under-proofed, starter weak, or water too low.  
Flat loaf: Over-proofed or shaping lacked tension.  
Sourness: Increase whole-grain %, extend fridge retard.  
Blowouts: Score deeper/more, or seam not sealed.

8. Variations
• Add-ins: 20 % nuts/seeds (soak first) or 15 % dried fruit.  
• Higher Hydration (75–80 %): Open crumb ciabatta-style.  
• Whole-Grain: Swap up to 50 % whole wheat/rye; increase water 5–10 %.  
• Pan‐loaf: Shape tighter, proof in greased loaf pan, bake without Dutch oven but add steam pan.

9. Storage
• Let loaf cool completely.  
• Store cut-side down in paper bag 24 h, then plastic for up to 4 days, or slice/freeze up to 1 month. Revive in 350 °F oven 10 min.

10. Safety & Hygiene
• Discard pink/orange starter (mold).  
• Use clean utensils; keep starter jar loosely covered to avoid pressure build-up.

By mastering the starter, controlling fermentation temperature, and practicing shaping and scoring, you’ll consistently produce artisanal sourdough with crackling crust and a flavorful, moist crumb.
